| L02 | I'd be inclined to… | *I'd be inclined to wait.* |

| L02 | not ideal | *It's not ideal, honestly.* |

| L03 | make a start | *I'll make a start this week.* |
| L03 | take a risk | *They weren't willing to take a risk.* |
| L03 | take the point | *She took the point about the workload.* |
| L03 | take responsibility | *He took responsibility for it.* |
| L03 | give it some thought | *She said she'd give it some thought.* |
| L03 | pay attention | *Nobody was paying attention.* |
| L03 | raise a concern | *She raised a couple of concerns.* |
| L03 | meet a deadline | *We met the deadline, just.* |

| L04 | *Listen — · Can I flag something? · Actually, before we get into that — · On a more serious note —* | **Open a gear change** |
| L04 | *I wanted to flag it before it comes up. · It's quite carefully worded, but…* | **Soften bad news at high stakes** |
| L04 | *That's not ideal. · That's a bit of a problem. · It's not great.* | **Understate** |
| L04 | *I'd guess it's coming from above her. · I don't think this is her doing.* | **Hedge an attribution** |
| L04 | *I appreciate that. · Thanks for telling me. · Good to know.* | **Acknowledge warmly** |
| L04 | *Anyway. · Right — let's pick it up after. · Coffee?* | **Close the serious part** |

## Unit 10 — Professional Communication

| Lesson | English | Example |
|---|---|---|
| L01 | Building on that… | *Building on that — the sign-off has to be immediate.* |
| L01 | My only worry is… | *My only worry is the review stage.* |
| L01 | Can I just come in on that? | *Sorry, can I just come in on that?* |
| L01 | Just on that point — | *Just on that point — it moves the date.* |
| L01 | Sorry to interrupt, but… | *Sorry to interrupt, but that changes the timeline.* |
| L01 | Just to clarify — | *Just to clarify — do you mean the 20th?* |
| L01 | When you say X, do you mean…? | *When you say scope, do you mean deliverables?* |
| L01 | Could you expand on that? | *Could you expand on that?* |
| L01 | I'd support that | *I'd support that.* |
| L01 | That's my read too | *That's my read too.* |
| L01 | Sorry, go on | *That's all — sorry, go on.* |
| L01 | Before we move on — | *Before we move on — one thing.* |
| L02 | *Last quarter we… · Why do…? · Our X has never been higher — and yet…* | **Hook** |
| L02 | *I want to cover three things: … · I'll look at X, Y and Z.* | **Roadmap** |
| L02 | *Firstly… · Let's start with… · The first thing is…* | **Open a point** |
| L02 | *So that's X. · That's the first point.* | **Close a point** |
| L02 | *Moving on to… · Which brings me to… · Turning to…* | **Transition** |
| L02 | *We trialled this… · To give you an example… · The figures show…* | **Evidence** |
| L02 | *That's a small sample. · I wouldn't over-claim it.* | **Hedge honestly** |
| L02 | *To sum up… · In short… · So: three things.* | **Summarise** |
| L02 | *What I'd like is… · My recommendation is… · What I'm proposing is…* | **Ask** |
| L02 | *Happy to take questions.* | **Close** |
| L03 | *How about…? · Would you be open to…? · What if we…? · One option would be…* | **Propose** |
| L03 | *What could you do by…? · What's the constraint? · What would you need?* | **Probe** |
| L03 | *If you can…, we could… · provided that… · as long as… · in exchange, I'd want…* | **Trade** |
| L03 | *I take your point. · That's fair. · I can see why that matters.* | **Acknowledge** |
| L03 | *I'd be willing to… · We could probably live with… · Let's meet in the middle.* | **Concede partly** |
| L03 | *I'd love to help, but I can't go below… · That's genuinely not possible. What I can do is…* | **Hold the limit** |
| L03 | *The reason that matters to us is… · If we do X, it's worse for both of us.* | **State the interest** |
| L03 | *So — X, Y and Z. Have I got that right? · Let me say that back.* | **Confirm** |
| L03 | *Done. · That works. · I'll put it in writing.* | **Close** |
| L04 | It's X from Y | *It's Karim from Meridian.* |
| L04 | I'm calling about… | *I'm calling about the March invoice.* |
| L04 | Is now a good time? | *Is now a good time?* |
| L04 | Have you got five minutes? | *Have you got five minutes?* |
| L04 | you're breaking up | *Sorry, you're breaking up a bit.* |
| L04 | Could you repeat that? | *Sorry, could you repeat the last part?* |
| L04 | bear with me one second | *Bear with me one second.* |
| L04 | So I'll… and you'll… | *So I'll resend it, and you'll confirm.* |
| L04 | I'll follow up with an email | *I'll follow up with an email.* |
| L04 | Just to confirm… | *Just to confirm what we agreed…* |
| L04 | Could you put me through? | *Could you put me through to finance?* |
| L04 | I'll get that over within the hour | *I'll get that over within the hour.* |

## Unit 11 — Abstract Topics & Debate

| Lesson | English | Example |
|---|---|---|
| L01 | *I don't know enough to be confident, but… · Off the top of my head… · I only know this second-hand.* | **Admit the limit** |
| L01 | *There are advantages and problems. · On balance… · The trade-off is…* | **Pros and cons** |
| L01 | *The pressure is coming from two directions. · The root cause is… · Which leads to…* | **Causes** |
| L01 | *In the short term… · In the longer run… · Eventually…* | **Time frames** |
| L01 | *Having said that… · The counter-argument would be… · Although in fairness…* | **Counter-consideration** |
| L01 | *I'd separate two things here. · That's a separate question. · It depends whether we mean X or Y.* | **Distinction** |
| L01 | *That's underrated. · I think that's overstated.* | **Correct the emphasis** |
| L01 | *The wider point is… · What's often missed is…* | **Zoom out** |
| L01 | *Although I could be completely wrong. · I'd have said the same about X in 2019.* | **Hedge the whole thing** |
| L02 | *My main point is… · What I'd argue is… · My position is…* | **Claim** |
| L02 | *The reason is… · The evidence for that is… · That's borne out by…* | **Evidence** |
| L02 | *And the second reason is… · There's also the fact that…* | **Second reason** |
| L02 | *To give you a specific example… · Concretely… · A case in point is…* | **Example** |
| L02 | *Now, the obvious objection is… · The counter-argument would be…* | **Raise the objection** |
| L02 | *And that's partly fair. But… · Which is true, except that…* | **Rebut** |
| L02 | *I wouldn't over-claim that. · That's the weakest part of my case.* | **Concede a limit** |
| L02 | *So my conclusion is… · Which is why I'd… · What follows from that is…* | **Conclusion** |
| L02 | *What I'd like us to do is… · So I'd propose…* | **Ask** |
| L03 | *That's a fair point about X. · You're right that Y.* | **Acknowledge specifically** |
| L03 | *…and yet · …but I'd still argue · What I'd say is…* | **Concede and hold** |
| L03 | *They do, yes — although… · That's true, except that…* | **Concede and reframe** |
| L03 | *But so does the alternative. · The current approach isn't free either.* | **Turn it around** |
| L03 | *That's a good point. I'd revise that to… · Let me change that.* | **Concede and revise** |
| L03 | *The principle stands but the mechanism doesn't. · I'd keep the aim, change the method.* | **Separate principle from mechanism** |
| L03 | *I'm dropping X. Y I'd still argue for.* | **Name what survived** |
| L03 | *Actually, that changes my view. · You've convinced me on that part.* | **Change your mind** |
| L03 | *Let me think for a second. · I want to answer that properly.* | **Buy a moment** |
| L03 | *That's the weakest part of my case.* | **Name the weakest link** |
| L04 | *How was…? · How's the week been? · Did you get away at all?* | **Small-talk opener** |
| L04 | *Exhausting how? · Did you get any time at all? · Whereabouts?* | **Follow up** |
| L04 | *Classic. · Same thing happened to me in… · I know that feeling.* | **Give something back** |
| L04 | *Speaking of which… · Which actually makes me wonder…* | **Pivot on their material** |
| L04 | *That reminds me… · Funnily enough…* | **Pivot on association** |
| L04 | *Actually, while we're on that… · Can I ask you something about that?* | **Pivot with permission** |
| L04 | *On a more serious note… · Genuinely asking…* | **Explicit gear change** |
| L04 | *What do you think? · Is that your experience? · Am I being unfair?* | **Hand it back** |
| L04 | *Anyway. · Right. · Fair enough.* | **Mark the return** |
| L04 | *I should let you get on. · Good to see you. · Let's pick it up next week.* | **Close** |

## Unit 12 — Putting It Together (B2) ⭐

| Lesson | English | Example |
|---|---|---|
| L01 | *I've been trying to… on and off, properly since…* | **perfect continuous** |
| L01 | *I've had four interviews and no offers.* | **perfect simple + quantity** |
| L01 | *I hadn't looked at… I hadn't spoken to…* | **past perfect** |
| L01 | *I'd been telling myself for weeks that…* | **past perfect continuous** |
| L01 | *If I'd done two hours of research, I'd probably have…* | **third conditional** |
| L01 | *If I'd started in 2023, I'd be somewhere else by now.* | **mixed conditional** |
| L01 | *They must have decided before I walked in.* | **past deduction** |
| L01 | *They can't have had budget approval.* | **present deduction** |
| L01 | *By the end of the year I'll have applied to about thirty.* | **future perfect** |
| L01 | *This time next spring I'll either be doing something different…* | **future continuous** |
| L01 | *I've been wrong about my own timeline every time, so I wouldn't put money on it.* | **hedge** |
| L02 | *The team wasn't formally notified until it had been implemented.* | **passive, agentless** |
| L02 | *That could have been handled rather differently.* | **modal passive** |
| L02 | *It's my understanding that the restructure was signed off in March.* | **reporting passive** |
| L02 | *We had the whole system audited before launch.* | **causative** |
| L02 | *Our new lead, whom I haven't yet met, inherited a team with no warning.* | **non-defining relative** |
| L02 | *The guy running it now is somebody I've never met.* | **reduced relative** |
| L02 | *She'd been in meetings about it for a month, which gives it away.* | ***which*** **for a whole idea** |
| L02 | *My manager has indicated that she wasn't consulted.* | **reporting verb + stance** |
| L02 | *My manager swore she didn't know either.* | **reporting verb, informal** |
| L02 | *I'd be cautious about drawing conclusions from that.* | **diplomatic hedge** |
| L02 | *My priority is making sure the handover doesn't lose momentum.* | **formal collocation** |
| L02 | *I'm keeping my head down until it settles.* | **informal collocation** |
| L03 | *— should have been checked, rather —* | **plain repair** |
| L03 | *sorry, been checked —* | **repair with a marker** |
| L03 | *or rather, what I mean is…* | **rephrase forward** |
| L03 | *— I keep doing that —* | **self-flag and continue** |
| L03 | *let me put that another way.* | **buy a beat, honestly** |
| L03 | *that's a good question, actually — give me a second.* | **hold the floor while you think** |
| L04 | *That's a good question — let me think about it for a second.* | **buy thinking time** |
| L04 | *I'll answer that from the work side, if that's alright.* | **narrow a huge question** |
| L04 | *There are two things going on here. The first is…* | **signpost an argument** |
| L04 | *You're right that it's expensive — I still think it's cheaper than the alternative.* | **concede, then hold** |
| L04 | *I'd be cautious about saying that, but my impression is…* | **hedge honestly** |
| L04 | *My manager has indicated that… — although I haven't seen it myself.* | **attribute a claim** |
| L04 | *It must have been decided earlier; nobody could answer about the start date.* | **speculate with evidence** |
| L04 | *If we'd started in March, we'd be finished by now.* | **an unreal alternative** |
| L04 | *If I were saying this to my director, I'd put it as…* | **shift register deliberately** |
| L04 | *Does it work the same way in your field?* | **ask a genuine question** |
| L04 | *Can I come back to what you said about deadlines?* | **pick up an earlier thread** |
| L04 | *— should have been checked, rather —* | **repair, mid-phrase** |
| L04 | *So, broadly, that's where I've landed on it.* | **close a long answer** |
